title: Three splits, one pattern
subtitle: Crashlytics/Performance (done), the native adapter (done), MoEngage (next). Same socket-and-plug idea, three different shapes of plug.

meta.description: Compares the three splits: two real plugs (Measure work), a real plug + a null plug (native adapter), and named slots with a no-op plug (MoEngage plan). Ends with the checklist and what crashes if you forget a step.

actors.name: Shared code
actors.explain: The class in services that needs the feature: Dio's provider, EventLoggerFactory, NotificationInboxService…

actors.name: Socket
actors.explain: The abstract class in services. Sometimes new (HttpAdapterProvider), sometimes already there (EventLogger, NotificationInbox).

actors.name: get_it
actors.explain: Connects each socket to the plug the running app registered.

actors.name: bonds_services
actors.explain: Real plugs with the real SDK: Firebase, Cronet, MoEngage (after the move).

actors.name: ultra_services
actors.explain: Ultra's plugs: sometimes a different real SDK (Measure), sometimes a 'nothing here' plug.

actors.name: The SDK
actors.explain: The third-party package that must stop shipping in ultra. It moves with the bonds plug.

steps.title: Same pattern, three times
steps.summary: Split 1 (Measure work): two real plugs, Firebase vs Measure. Split 2 (native adapter): a real plug vs a 'null' plug. Split 3 (MoEngage, next): the sockets already exist, but they're named slots, and ultra needs a do-nothing plug in each.
steps.oneliner: What changes between splits is only the shape of ultra's plug.

steps.title: Split 1: two real plugs (done, cb7038e3)
steps.summary: CrashlyticsService and PerformanceService became abstract in services. Bonds plugs in Firebase, ultra plugs in Measure. Both apps really use the feature, just with different SDKs.
steps.oneliner: Both apps need the feature → two real plugs.

messages.label: PerformanceService
messages.why: A socket with four methods, one of which even returns a Dio piece (an interceptor). Each app builds it with its own SDK.

notes.23: Bonds returns a Firebase interceptor, ultra a Measure one.

messages.label: Firebase Crashlytics + Performance
messages.why: Their pubspec lines moved from services to bonds_services in the same commit.

messages.label: Measure
messages.why: measure_flutter and measure_dio live only in ultra_services' pubspec.

steps.title: Split 2: a real plug and a null plug (done, 89a6247a)
steps.summary: A brand-new socket, HttpAdapterProvider. Bonds' plug builds Cronet/NSURLSession. Ultra doesn't want a native engine at all, so its plug returns null, meaning 'keep Dio's default'. The caller handles null.
steps.oneliner: Only one app needs the feature → design the socket so 'nothing' is a valid answer.

messages.label: createAdapter() → adapter or null
messages.why: The nullable return type is the design choice that keeps ultra's plug to one line and removes the isBondsApp check from services.

notes.13: Shared constant both sides use (plan B).

messages.label: DefaultHttpAdapterProvider → null
messages.why: A plug that exists only to fill the socket. Without it, get_it has nothing registered and the first network call crashes.

notes.6: Same registration line as any real plug.

messages.label: native_dio_adapter
messages.why: The one pubspec line that moved. Ultra's dependency tree no longer has it (checked with pub deps).

steps.title: Split 3a (next): MoEngage events, a named slot
steps.summary: The socket already exists: EventLogger. But EventLoggerFactory asks for four of them, told apart by name. MoEngage's logger is registered in services today. Plan: move it to bonds_services, and give ultra a do-nothing logger under the same name.
steps.oneliner: Named slot → ultra must fill that exact name, or the app crashes at startup.

messages.label: @Named('MoEngageEventLogger')
messages.why: New term: named slot. When one socket type is plugged several times, @Named picks which one. Like Hilt's @Named qualifier. Each name is its own slot that must be filled.

notes.9: This slot is the one to fill differently per app.
notes.15: Same socket type as the other three: EventLogger.

messages.label: today: MoEngageEventLogger in services
messages.why: Registered in the shared package, so moengage_flutter ships to ultra. This is the plug that moves to bonds_services.

notes.3: The SDK import that leaks into ultra.
notes.7: A factory plug for the EventLogger socket.

messages.label: plan: no-op logger, same name
messages.why: Decision still open (handoff 2b): a do-nothing EventLogger in ultra_services named 'MoEngageEventLogger' (recommended), or make the factory's slot optional. CtaService is built eagerly and needs this factory, so a missing slot means a startup crash.

steps.title: Split 3b (next): MoEngage inbox, a named slot + a lifetime fix
steps.summary: Same shape: NotificationInbox socket, @Named('MoengageInbox') slot. Two extra things: MoengageInbox is an eager @Singleton (must become @LazySingleton once it lives in bonds_services), and NotificationInboxService still checks isBondsApp.
steps.oneliner: When a plug moves to a per-app package, check its lifetime: eager plugs there crash on the module order.

messages.label: @Named('MoengageInbox') + isBondsApp
messages.why: Two inbox slots, plus an app check in shared code. Once each app plugs its own inbox, that check may not be needed any more (a later decision).

notes.21: Another 'which app am I?' in the shared package.

messages.label: today: eager @Singleton in services
messages.why: Eager = built during getIt.init(), as soon as it's registered. In services that works. In bonds_services, which registers first, its dependency (EnvironmentConfig) wouldn't exist yet → crash. So it moves as @LazySingleton.

notes.5: moengage_inbox SDK, shipped to ultra today.
notes.13: Eager. Must become @LazySingleton when it moves.

messages.label: plan: empty inbox (or a new one)
messages.why: Decision still open (handoff 2c): an empty inbox under 'MoengageInbox', or a renamed/new inbox design (you lean 'new one').

steps.title: The checklist for any split
steps.summary: 1) Which SDK leaks into the other app? 2) Is there a socket already, or do I make one? Named? 3) Bonds' plug. 4) Ultra's plug: real, null, or no-op? 5) Lifetime: lazy in per-app packages. 6) Move the pubspec line. 7) Regenerate, then check the dependency tree.
steps.oneliner: Forget a plug → 'not registered' crash. Eager plug in a per-app package → startup crash. Forget the pubspec → the SDK still ships.

messages.label: missing plug → crash
messages.why: get_it throws 'Object/factory with type X is not registered' the moment anything asks. For eagerly built services that's during startup, so the app never opens.

messages.label: why per-app goes first
messages.why: The comment in both injector.dart files: services eagerly builds DeepLinkService, which needs CrashlyticsService, so the per-app module must already be registered. And that's exactly why everything in it must be lazy.

notes.14: The reason for the order, written down.
